I think pretty much the general conclusion is that New Vegas has better story/game mechanics, but Fallout 3 has better atmosphere.

The trouble with New Vegas is it does railroad the crap out of things for the first few hours. After that it really opens up though. The key is to complete quests; not just wander around aimlessly shooting and looting. I think the difference between people who love NV and 3 are those who love NV take the time to get entrenched in the world and characters; whereas those who prefer 3 just came to shoot and loot around interesting and varied environments.

I personally got way more involved in New Vegas than 3; mostly because the story in Fallout 3 is absolute tripe compared to New Vegas. This is a great article about the many reasons Fallout 3 is fun, but void of any actual world. FO3 is an interesting shooting gallery, and not much else.

Also I never got anything out of the intro/growing up part of 3; New Vegas allowed me to make my own backstory up (for the most part; you're always a courier in NV), but in 3 you're always a sheltered vault child with a fairly good childhood. It's just hard for me to play an evil character if I know I grew up with a loving father and stable environment; serial killers usually come from broken homes (in my mind, at least).

Lastly New Vegas' mechanics just work better to me. You can kill any character in NV; literally any character (except one that drives the main plot, to be fair). FO3 does the same thing as Oblivion and Skyrim (which I think is so lame) where if you kill someone that screws up the main quest they just fall asleep for 6 seconds and come back with full health. That is incredibly immersion breaking, it is insane to me that Bethesda continues to do this rather than find simple workarounds (NV usually just has the quest break, but I'd rather a quest break than have 1/10 characters be immortal).

Also I think people who disliked NV and didn't give it more than a few hours just didn't like being weak. In the beginning of NV (and honestly kind of through the whole thing) you're pretty weak. In 3 you can fight a Deathclaw level 2 without much problem; in New Vegas you simply can't fight them unless you're of a decent level (at least 10, possibly 20). Yeah it means you can't wander anywhere at level 1, but it makes sense. Why would I, a previously sheltered vault dweller, just wander into the wastes at total random? I've never left my precious vault, and now I'm gonna tackle irradiated beasts and monsters at the start? It just seems kind of crazy. In NV I can say "Okay well I've been shot in the gosh darn head, I'd better take the safest routes to kill that Benny jerk so I don't actually die this time." What I mean is that's what happens naturally; I can try to go the unsafe ways, but I get destroyed as I should. Why would a recovering gunshot victim be able to wander the post-apocalypse wasteland immediately after waking up?

That's my main point I guess; FO3 just doesn't add up when I really think about it, and NV does. Even just the basic "what do they eat" question fails miserably in FO3, and never fails in NV. FO3 also has crazy stuff like NPC's who stand in/near radiation 24/7 but are totally fine (lookin' at you Megaton Church of the Atom or whatever they're called).

Sorry I know this has been a rambling unfocused post, but I just can't understand people who get more immersed in FO3. New Vegas has memorable characters; robosexuals, alcoholic caravaneers, casino gangs, an immortal 200 year old man who controls Vegas from a computer, and most importantly it all kinda makes sense. In FO3 I can kill 1000 innocent people, but if I donate enough bottled water I'm a nice guy again! In NV your bad actions are seen alongside your good ones; and if you max out the bad reputation and good reputation people don't know what to expect, and won't trust you. That makes sense to me; if I help rebuild a town and then kill 3 people I'm not "even" karmically or with the people I interacted with; I'm a lunatic who no one can understand.
